messages.subject: Interpreting blavCompare output
parts:
I am having trouble interpreting the output when comparing two models. Below is my code and the output for the compares. I am mainly confused because when I swap the objects the outputs for the waic and loo remain the same. I assumed it would switch from negative to positive like the Laplace approximation. Please let me know if there is an error in my code or i am interpreting the outputs incorrectly. Thanks!

saturatedmodel <- 'Forage Fish Community Dynamics =~ abundanceforg+shanforg+evenforg+richforg
               Sport Fish Community Dynamics =~ abundancesport+shansport+evensport+richsport
              Water Quality =~ chlaugl+Temperature+DissolvedO2+pH+Salinity'

DMalt.model <- 'Forage Fish Community Dynamics =~ abundanceforg+shanforg+richforg
               Sport Fish Community Dynamics =~ abundancesport+shansport+richsport
              Water Quality =~ Temperature+Salinity+DissolvedO2'

satmod.NBdecmar<-bcfa(saturatedmodel, data = NBdecmar, meanstructure = T )
DMalt.NBdecmar<-bcfa(DMalt.model, data = NBdecmar, meanstructure = T )

blavCompare(satmod.NBdecmar,DMalt.NBdecmar)
Output: 
WAIC difference & SE (positive values favor object2): 
 -711.890   61.847 

LOO difference & SE (positive values favor object2): 
 -705.069   59.558 

Laplace approximation to the log-Bayes factor
(experimental; positive values favor object1): -5486.949 

blavCompare(DMalt.NBdecmar,satmod.NBdecmar)
Output:
WAIC difference & SE (positive values favor object2): 
 -711.890   61.847 

LOO difference & SE (positive values favor object2): 
 -705.069   59.558 

Laplace approximation to the log-Bayes factor
(experimental; positive values favor object1): 5486.949

messages.subject: Re: Interpreting blavCompare output
parts:
Dakota

Thank you for noticing this.

This is not a bug, but we do need to take out the message (positive values favor object2), I will do this change for the next update, or add the IC to the default output

Just went back through the function, and this lack of changed sign is coming from the loo_compare function from the loo package. We use that package to do the heavy lifting. Aparently in the last update the loo_compare function doesnt change signs, it appears it arrange them before comparison.

I would recommend you to save the blavCompare object, as the saved object contains the loo and waic estimates for both models. Then can see which ones have lower LOO and WAIC

bc1 <- blavCompare(satmod.NBdecmar,DMalt.NBdecmar)
bc1
bc1$loo
bc1$waic
